literature.japan_paper: Andersen, Todorov & Ubukata (2021), Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.07.005
literature.source_method_paper: Bollerslev, Todorov & Xu (2015), Journal of Financial Economics, DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2015.02.010
literature.japan_target_finding: For yen-denominated Nikkei 225 excess returns, LJV-US is described as moderate/less-than-compelling; significance is strongest around 5-8 month horizons. Dollar-denominated Nikkei predictability is materially stronger.
literature.timing_guardrail: The Japan paper excludes the last U.S. trading day of each month when constructing U.S. predictors because Japan closes before U.S. month-end information is available.

public_author_data.identity_check: For the original 1996-Aug-2013 sample, public series mean*100=0.4547 and stdev*100=0.5449, closely matching the published 2015 LJV summary statistics (mean 0.45, stdev 0.54), supporting that this is the authors' LJV series.

data_lineage.raw_options_origin: The 2015 paper states raw S&P 500 option closing bid/ask data came from OptionMetrics.
data_lineage.public_series_value: Author-provided derived LJV history can support historical method/series replication without repurchasing raw OptionMetrics for that old interval.
data_lineage.remaining_blocker: Series ends in May 2017, before the 2021 Japan paper publication. It therefore cannot provide a genuine post-publication OOS predictor sample. Extending the same LJV measure after 2017 still requires new rights-clean deep-OTM SPX option data or an independently published continuation.

reopen_rule: Reopen only if a rights-clean continuation of the same/sufficiently equivalent LJV measure supplies genuinely new post-publication observations and the yen-denominated JNU/Nikkei target/horizon is preregistered without mining.

findings.source: Andersen, Todorov & Ubukata (2021), Journal of Econometrics
findings.meaning: The Japanese-equity paper itself extends its source data beyond the public author LJV workbook, but does not provide a verified self-service public post-publication continuation.

findings.source: Jacobs, Ke & Pan (2026), JFQA, Tail Risk Around FOMC Announcements
findings.meaning: The paper reports Bollerslev-et-al.-style 7-day LJV/RJV through 2021 and has supplementary material, demonstrating methodological continuation. No downloadable raw LJV time series suitable for our replication was verified in this search.

findings.coverage: Japanese option-implied LJV illustrated through March 2024
findings.meaning: Useful evidence that the LJV concept remains computable in Japan, but it is Japan-specific LJV and cannot substitute for the U.S. LJV predictor emphasized by Andersen et al. for Japanese returns.

findings.source: Suh, Yoo & Yoon (2021), Journal of Futures Markets
findings.coverage: Paper reports S&P 500 option-derived tail-risk indexes
findings.meaning: Data availability says available from corresponding author upon reasonable request, not a verified free self-service dataset; measures are not automatically equivalent to the Andersen/Bollerslev U.S. LJV series.

continuation_search.postpublication_requirement: For a formal new directional family, obtain enough genuinely post-2021 U.S. LJV observations under rights-clean access to support the preregistered yen-denominated Japanese/JNU horizon. Historical 1996-2017/2018 replication alone has no promotion power.
prohibited_substitutions: other tail-risk index without an independently justified new family
